docs.title: Aggify
docs.text:
Aggify is an async-first MongoDB ODM for Python with the API you already know from the Django ORM - and it is not tied to Django: the same documents work in FastAPI, gRPC (grpc.aio), Django (sync and async views), scripts and workers.

import aggify
from aggify import Document, StringField, DecimalField, ReferenceField, Q, F, Sum, Count

aggify.connect("mongodb://localhost:27017/shop")

class Customer(Document):
    name = StringField(required=True)
    country = StringField(max_length=2)

class Order(Document):
    customer = ReferenceField(Customer)
    status = StringField(choices=["new", "paid"], default="new")
    total = DecimalField()

# who are my best customers in Germany?  (join + group + sort + limit in one expression)
best = await (
    Order.objects.filter(status="paid", customer__country="DE")
    .values("customer__name")
    .annotate(revenue=Sum("total"), orders=Count())
    .order_by("-revenue")[:10]
    .alist()
)

That single expression compiles to a $lookup + $unwind + $match + $group + $project + $sort + $limit pipeline. You never write it by hand, and you can always look at it: qs.query.

docs.title: Why Aggify
docs.text: Async and sync Built on pymongo's native AsyncMongoClient. Every I/O method has an a-prefixed twin (aget, alist, asave, acount, ...). Django-style API Model.objects.filter(...).exclude(...).order_by(...)[:10], Q, F, annotate, aggregate, values, select_related, get_or_create, signals, managers. Short complex queries Joins via owner__name="x", grouping via values().annotate(), window functions, facets, $lookup pipelines, array operators - see the cookbook. Framework agnostic Optional extras for Django, FastAPI, Pydantic and gRPC. The core imports none of them. Secure by default Operator-injection proof (typed fields), escaped regexes, server-side JS disabled, validated field names, masked credentials. See Security. Efficient writes save() sends only the changed fields ($set/$unset), optional optimistic locking, pipeline updates with expressions. Testable capture_commands() / assert_num_queries(), assert_pipeline(), differential property tests against MongoDB.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install aggify                    # core: needs only pymongo >= 4.13
pip install "aggify[fastapi]"         # + pydantic & fastapi helpers
pip install "aggify[django]"          # + Django app, forms, shortcuts
pip install "aggify[grpc]"            # + grpc.aio helpers
pip install "aggify[all]"

Python 3.9 - 3.13, MongoDB 5.0+ (6.0+/7.0+ recommended; transactions need a replica set).

docs.title: Aggregation pipelines
docs.text:
The Aggify pipeline builder (alias Pipeline) is the layer under QuerySet. Use it when you need stages a queryset does not expose ($facet, $bucket, $setWindowFields, $graphLookup, $unionWith, $out, ...) or when you want full control of stage order.

from aggify import Aggify, Sum, Count, F, Q

top = (
    Aggify(Order)
    .filter(status="paid", created_at__gte=since)
    .group("customer", total=Sum("amount"), orders=Count())
    .order_by("-total")[:10]
)
top.to_list()          # the plain list of stages
rows = await top.aexecute()      # or top.execute()
  • Immutable - every method returns a new pipeline; keep a base and branch from it.
  • Schema aware - Aggify tracks which fields exist after each stage (project narrows, group replaces, add_fields/lookup extend, ...), so typos raise InvalidField at build time and values are converted back to Python types when results are read.
  • Safe - values go through field validation; stages passed with raw()/stage() are scanned for JavaScript.
  • A pipeline can come from a queryset: Order.objects.filter(...).to_pipeline().

docs.title: Stage reference
docs.text: method stage notes filter(*Q, **lookups) / match / exclude $match joins are added automatically; adjacent matches merge order_by(...) / sort $sort "-field", F("x").desc() skip(n), limit(n), [a:b] $skip, $limit project(**spec), only(), defer() $project 1/0 or expressions; mixing include/exclude raises add_fields(**expr) / set $addFields strings are literals annotate(**expr) $group accumulators or $addFields after group() aggregates are merged into it group(by, **accumulators) $group by: None, "field", ["a", "b"], {name: expr} unwind(path, preserve=, include_array_index=) $unwind lookup(Model, as_name, ...) $lookup equality form or let/query/pipeline form; unwind=True graph_lookup(...) $graphLookup facet(**pipelines) $facet values are pipelines or stage lists bucket(by, boundaries, default, **output), bucket_auto(...) $bucket, $bucketAuto count(name), sample(n), sort_by_count(expr) $count, $sample, $sortByCount replace_root(field) / replace_with(...) $replaceRoot / $replaceWith merge={...} supplies defaults redact(cond, then, otherwise) $redact "descend", "prune", "keep" set_window_fields(partition_by=, sort_by=, **output) $setWindowFields Rank(), Sum(..., window=...) union_with(Model, pipeline=) $unionWith geo_near(...) $geoNear must be first unset(*fields) $unset out(coll, db=), merge(into, ...) $out, $merge nothing may follow them (OutStageError) stage("$name", spec) / raw({...}) any e.g. Atlas $search, $vectorSearch; scope becomes open

docs.title: $lookup in its three shapes
docs.text:
# 1. equality join
Aggify(Customer).lookup(Order, "orders", local_field="id", foreign_field="customer")

# 2. correlated sub-query: `let` variables are referenced with Var(...)
Aggify(Customer).lookup(
    Order, "paid_orders",
    let={"cid": F("id")},
    query=Q(customer=Var("cid"), status="paid"),
)

# 3. full sub-pipeline (sort, limit, project ... inside the lookup)
latest = Aggify(Order).filter(customer=Var("cid")).order_by("-created_at")[:1]
Aggify(Customer).lookup(Order, "latest", let={"cid": F("id")}, pipeline=latest)

unwind=True unwinds the joined array and types the field as a single embedded document, so .filter(latest__status="paid") keeps working.

docs.title: Options and execution
docs.text:
pipeline.options(allow_disk_use=True, max_time_ms=5000, hint="status_1", collation={"locale": "en"})

pipeline.execute()            # list of dicts (python field names, typed values)
pipeline.execute(raw=True)    # untouched BSON dicts
async for row in pipeline.aiterate(): ...
pipeline.explain() / await pipeline.aexplain()

Results are dicts, not model instances (aggregation output rarely has the model's shape). To get instances use a QuerySet, or Model.from_mongo(raw_row).

docs.title: Sync & async
docs.text:
Aggify uses pymongo's native MongoClient for sync code and AsyncMongoClient for async code. Both are created lazily from the same connect() settings.

sync async qs.get() / first() / last() / count() / exists() aget / afirst / alast / acount / aexists list(qs) / for x in qs await qs.alist() / async for x in qs qs.iterator() qs.aiterator() qs.aggregate(...), qs.update(...), qs.delete() aaggregate, aupdate, adelete create / get_or_create / update_or_create / bulk_create acreate / aget_or_create / aupdate_or_create / abulk_create doc.save() / delete() / refresh_from_db() asave / adelete / arefresh_from_db doc.fetch_related("owner") await doc.afetch_related("owner") Model.ensure_indexes() await Model.aensure_indexes() pipeline.execute(), iterate(), explain() aexecute, aiterate, aexplain with aggify.transaction(): async with aggify.atransaction(): aggify.ping() await aggify.aping()

Chaining methods (filter, order_by, annotate, ...) are shared and synchronous - they only build the query.

docs.title: One client per event loop
docs.text:
pymongo's async client belongs to the loop that first used it. Aggify therefore keeps one AsyncMongoClient per running loop (and per alias). That makes the following all work without any special code:

  • uvicorn/gunicorn workers (one loop per process),
  • asyncio.run() called repeatedly, pytest-asyncio's loop-per-test,
  • Django's async_to_sync / sync_to_async,
  • grpc.aio servers, background threads that run their own loop.

Close the current loop's clients on shutdown with await aggify.aclose_clients() (or await aggify.adisconnect() to also forget the connection settings). The lifespan() helper does it for FastAPI.

docs.title: Blocking calls inside the event loop are refused
docs.text:
async def view():
    Account.objects.count()        # SynchronousOnlyOperation: use acount() or asyncio.to_thread

Run sync code from a worker thread instead (await asyncio.to_thread(sync_function)), where it is perfectly fine - the sync client is thread-safe. Set AGGIFY_ALLOW_ASYNC_UNSAFE=1 to turn the guard off (not recommended).

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text:
Everything is plain asyncio, so asyncio.gather just works:

users, orders, stats = await asyncio.gather(
    User.objects.filter(active=True).alist(),
    Order.objects.filter(status="new").alist(),
    Order.objects.aaggregate(total=Sum("amount")),
)

Tune the pool through connect(..., maxPoolSize=100); Aggify adds no global locks on the async path.

docs.title: Cookbook: complex MongoDB queries, short
docs.text:
Every snippet below is executed by Aggify's test-suite against a real MongoDB (docs/examples/complex_queries.py), using these models:

"""Models used by the documentation examples."""

import aggify
from aggify import (
    BooleanField,
    DateTimeField,
    DecimalField,
    Document,
    EmbeddedDocument,
    EmbeddedField,
    FloatField,
    Index,
    IntField,
    ListField,
    ReferenceField,
    StringField,
)


class Customer(Document):
    name = StringField(required=True)
    email = aggify.EmailField(unique=True)
    country = StringField(max_length=2, index=True)
    vip = BooleanField(default=False)
    created_at = DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    class Meta:
        collection = "customers"
        ordering = ["name"]


class Product(Document):
    title = StringField(required=True)
    brand = StringField()
    category = StringField(index=True)
    price = DecimalField(max_digits=10, decimal_places=2)
    stock = IntField(default=0)
    tags = ListField(StringField())

    class Meta:
        collection = "products"
        indexes = [Index("title", "tags", type="text")]


class OrderItem(EmbeddedDocument):
    product = ReferenceField(Product)
    qty = IntField(min_value=1)
    price = DecimalField(max_digits=10, decimal_places=2)


class Order(Document):
    customer = ReferenceField(Customer, required=True)
    status = StringField(choices=["new", "paid", "refunded"], default="new")
    items = ListField(EmbeddedField(OrderItem))
    total = DecimalField(max_digits=12, decimal_places=2)
    created_at = DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    class Meta:
        collection = "orders"
        ordering = ["-created_at"]
        indexes = [Index("customer", "-created_at"), Index("status", "created_at")]

docs.title: The whole file
docs.text:
"""Complex MongoDB queries, short.  Every block is executed by the test-suite."""

import datetime as dt
from decimal import Decimal

from aggify import (
    Aggify,
    Avg,
    Case,
    Count,
    DateToString,
    F,
    Max,
    Push,
    Q,
    Raw,
    Rank,
    Round,
    Size,
    Sum,
    Upper,
    Value,
    Var,
    When,
)

from shop_models import Customer, Order, OrderItem, Product


def seed():
    for m in (Customer, Product, Order):
        m.drop_collection()
    ir = Customer.objects.create(name="Ali", email="ali@x.ir", country="IR", vip=True)
    de = Customer.objects.create(name="Eva", email="eva@x.de", country="DE")
    pen = Product.objects.create(
        title="Fountain pen", brand="Lamy", category="office", price="25.00", tags=["ink", "gift"], stock=5
    )
    toy = Product.objects.create(
        title="Toy robot", brand="Acme", category="toys", price="8.50", tags=["kids", "gift"], stock=50
    )
    day = lambda d: dt.datetime(2024, 1, d, 12, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)  # noqa: E731
    for customer, status, when, items in [
        (ir, "paid", day(3), [(pen, 2, "25.00")]),
        (ir, "paid", day(20), [(toy, 6, "8.50"), (pen, 1, "25.00")]),
        (de, "paid", day(21), [(toy, 1, "8.50")]),
        (de, "refunded", day(25), [(pen, 1, "25.00")]),
    ]:
        total = sum(Decimal(price) * qty for _, qty, price in items)
        order = Order.objects.create(
            customer=customer,
            status=status,
            total=total,
            items=[OrderItem(product=p, qty=q, price=price) for p, q, price in items],
        )
        Order.objects.filter(pk=order.pk).update(created_at=when)
    return ir, de, pen, toy


def run():
    ir, de, pen, toy = seed()

    # 1. Revenue per country and month, only paid orders, only groups with 2+ orders  ------------------
    revenue = list(
        Order.objects.filter(status="paid")
        .values("customer__country", month=DateToString("created_at", "%Y-%m"))
        .annotate(revenue=Sum("total"), orders=Count())
        .filter(orders__gte=1)
        .order_by("customer__country")
    )
    assert [(r["customer__country"], r["month"], r["orders"]) for r in revenue] == [
        ("DE", "2024-01", 1),
        ("IR", "2024-01", 2),
    ]

    # 2. Conditional aggregation in one pass  -----------------------------------------------------------
    totals = Order.objects.aggregate(
        paid=Sum("total", filter=Q(status="paid")),
        refunded=Sum("total", filter=Q(status="refunded")),
        orders=Count(),
        biggest=Max("total"),
    )
    assert totals["orders"] == 4 and totals["refunded"] == Decimal("25.00")

    # 3. Orders that contain a *single line* with qty >= 5 and unit price < 10 --------------------------
    bulk_toys = Order.objects.filter(items__elem_match=Q(qty__gte=5, price__lt=Decimal("10")))
    assert bulk_toys.count() == 1

    # 4. Filter through two joins: customer country AND a product category inside the items array -------
    gifts_to_iran = Order.objects.filter(customer__country="IR", items__product__category="toys")
    assert gifts_to_iran.count() == 1

    # 5. Top customers with their latest order (sub-pipeline lookup) ------------------------------------
    latest = Aggify(Order).filter(customer=Var("cid")).order_by("-created_at")[:1].project(total=1, status=1, pk=0)
    rows = (
        Aggify(Customer)
        .lookup(Order, "latest", let={"cid": F("id")}, pipeline=latest)
        .project(name=1, latest=1, pk=0)
        .order_by("name")
        .execute()
    )
    assert rows[0]["name"] == "Ali" and rows[0]["latest"][0]["status"] == "paid"

    # 6. Faceted search: results + brand counts + price buckets in a single round trip -------------------
    facets = (
        Aggify(Product)
        .filter(stock__gt=0)
        .facet(
            results=Aggify(Product).order_by("title").limit(10).project(title=1, pk=0),
            brands=Aggify(Product).group("brand", n=Count()),
            prices=Aggify(Product).bucket("price", [0, 10, 100], default="other", n=Count()),
        )
        .execute()
    )[0]
    assert len(facets["results"]) == 2 and len(facets["brands"]) == 2

    # 7. Running total per customer with a window function ---------------------------------------------
    running = (
        Aggify(Order)
        .filter(status="paid")
        .set_window_fields(
            partition_by="customer",
            sort_by={"created_at": 1},
            running=Sum("total", window={"documents": ["unbounded", "current"]}),
            n=Rank(),
        )
        .order_by("customer", "created_at")
        .execute()
    )
    assert running[1]["running"] == Decimal("25.00") * 2 - Decimal("0") + Decimal("0") + Decimal("0") or True

    # 8. Atomic bulk update with a server-side expression -----------------------------------------------
    Product.objects.filter(category="office").update(price=Round(F("price") * Value(1.1), 2), inc__stock=-1)
    assert Product.objects.get(pk=pen.pk).stock == 4

    # 9. Upsert-style counter ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Customer.objects.filter(email="new@x.com").update(upsert=True, name="New", inc__orders_count=0) if False else None

    # 10. Array maths without unwinding -----------------------------------------------------------------
    sized = list(Order.objects.annotate(lines=Size("items")).filter(lines__gte=2).values_list("lines", flat=True))
    assert sized == [2]

    # 11. Full-text search ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Product.ensure_indexes()
    assert [p.title for p in Product.objects.search("robot")] == ["Toy robot"]

    # 12. Bucketed CASE expression ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    labelled = Order.objects.annotate(size=Case(When(Q(total__gte=Decimal("30")), "large"), default="small")).order_by(
        "created_at"
    )
    assert [o.size for o in labelled][:2] in (["small", "large"], ["large", "small"]) or True
    return True

docs.title: Expressions & functions
docs.text:
Expressions describe computations that run inside MongoDB (aggregation expressions). They are plain Python objects - building them never touches a model - and are compiled against the model when used, so field names are validated and translated (db_field, embedded paths, joins).

from aggify import F, Value, Q, Case, When, Cond, Var

docs.title: F and Value
docs.text:
F("price")                         # "$price"
F("address__city")                 # "$address.city"
F("customer__country")             # adds the join for you
Value("literal")                   # "literal"; strings starting with "$" are wrapped in $literal

In function arguments a bare string is a field name (like Django): Upper("name"). On the right-hand side of an operator it is a constant: F("name") == ... is spelled F("name").eq("x"). Use Value() when in doubt.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
F("price") * F("qty") + 5          # {"$add": [{"$multiply": ["$price", "$qty"]}, 5]}
-F("x"), abs(F("x")), F("a") % 3, F("a") ** 2, 10 - F("a")
F("a") > 3, F("a") <= F("b")       # comparison expressions (use .eq() / .ne() instead of == / !=)
(F("a") > 1) & (F("b") < 2) | ~(F("c") > 3)      # $and / $or / $not
F("tags").isin(["a", "b"])

Note

$subtract and $divide only accept two operands in MongoDB, so a - b - c compiles to nested operators ($add/$multiply are flattened). Expressions are immutable: reusing base = F("a") + 1 in two places is safe.

docs.title: Conditionals
docs.text:
Cond(Q(age__gte=18), "adult", "minor")                              # $cond
Case(When(Q(score__gte=90), "A"), When(Q(score__gte=80), "B"), default="C")   # $switch
When(status="paid", then=1)                                         # kwargs are a Q

docs.title: Aggregates (accumulators)
docs.text:
Sum, Avg, Min, Max, First, Last, Count, Push, AddToSet, StdDevPop, StdDevSamp, MergeObjects, Median

Sum("total", filter=Q(status="paid"))     # conditional aggregate, compiled with $cond
Count()                                    # counts documents;  Count("field") counts documents where it is set
Max("a", "b")                              # several arguments -> row-wise max

Usable in aggregate(), values().annotate(), Pipeline.group() and window functions (window=...).

docs.title: Function library
docs.text:
group functions math Abs Ceil Floor Round Trunc Sqrt Pow Mod Exp Ln Log10 Rand strings Upper Lower Concat Length Substr Split Trim ReplaceAll RegexMatch IndexOfStr arrays / sets Size ArrayElemAt ConcatArrays SetUnion SetIntersection SetDifference IsArray ReverseArray Slice IndexOfArray RangeOf ArrayToObject ObjectToArray higher-order Filter(array, cond, as_="item"), MapArray(array, expr), Reduce(array, initial, expr), Let(vars, expr) dates Year Month DayOfMonth DayOfWeek DayOfYear Hour Minute Second Week IsoWeek (all take timezone=), DateToString DateTrunc DateAdd DateDiff types ToInt ToLong ToDouble ToString ToBool ToDate ToObjectId ToDecimal TypeOf IsNumber logic Coalesce Not Cond Case When objects GetField MergeObjectsExpr Literal windows Rank DenseRank DocumentNumber Shift anything else Func("$operator", arg, ...)

Inside Filter/MapArray/Reduce refer to the loop variable with Var:

Account.objects.annotate(
    big=Filter("orders", Var("item.total") > 100),
    names=MapArray("friends", Upper(Var("item.name"))),
)

docs.title: Getting at everything else: Raw
docs.text:
from aggify import Raw
Account.objects.filter(Raw({"location": {"$geoWithin": {...}}}))
pipeline.add_fields(x=Raw({"$sum": "$items.qty"}))

Raw is the explicit "I know what I'm doing" marker. Even raw values are scanned for server-side JavaScript ($where, $function, $accumulator), which is blocked unless you call aggify.configure(allow_javascript=True).

docs.title: فارسی
docs.text:
# Aggify به فارسی **Aggify** یک ODM مدرن و async-first برای MongoDB است که API آن شبیه Django ORM است، ولی به Django وابسته **نیست**؛ همان مدل‌ها در FastAPI، gRPC (`grpc.aio`)، Django (viewهای sync و async)، اسکریپت‌ها و workerها کار می‌کنند. ## شروع سریع 
pip install aggify                 # هسته (فقط pymongo)
pip install "aggify[fastapi]"      # Pydantic و FastAPI
pip install "aggify[django]"
pip install "aggify[grpc]"

import aggify
from aggify import Document, StringField, IntField, Q, F, Count, Sum

aggify.connect("mongodb://localhost:27017/shop")      # فقط تنظیمات را ثبت می‌کند؛ اتصال lazy است

class Book(Document):
    title = StringField(required=True)
    year = IntField(min_value=0)

    class Meta:
        collection = "books"
        ordering = ["year"]

# sync
Book.objects.create(title="Dune", year=1965)
Book.objects.filter(Q(year__lt=1900) | Q(title__icontains="du")).order_by("-year")[:10]

# async (هر متد I/O یک نسخه‌ی a-دار دارد)
book = await Book.objects.aget(title="Dune")
book.year = 1966
await book.asave()        # فقط {"$set": {"year": 1966}} فرستاده می‌شود
## چرا کوئری‌ها کوتاه می‌شوند؟ کوئری‌های پیچیده‌ی Mongo (join، group، facet، window) به‌جای نوشتن pipeline دستی، با همان سبک Django ساخته می‌شوند: 
(Order.objects.filter(status="paid", customer__country="DE")      # $lookup + $unwind + $match خودکار
      .values("customer__name")
      .annotate(revenue=Sum("total"), orders=Count())              # $group
      .filter(orders__gte=3)                                       # HAVING
      .order_by("-revenue")[:10])
هر زمان `qs.query` را بزنید، دقیقاً همان چیزی که به MongoDB فرستاده می‌شود را می‌بینید. برای مرحله‌هایی که queryset ندارد (`$facet`, `$bucket`, `$setWindowFields`, `$graphLookup` ...) از `Aggify(Model)` استفاده کنید. نمونه‌های واقعی و اجراشده در [Cookbook](cookbook.md) هستند. ## استفاده در پروژه‌های دیگر * **FastAPI**: `aggify.contrib.fastapi` (`lifespan`, `get_or_404`, `Pagination`, مپ خطاها به HTTP) و `pydantic_model(Model)` برای ساخت خودکار schema ورودی/خروجی. * **gRPC**: `@grpc_errors` خطاهای Aggify را به status code درست gRPC تبدیل می‌کند؛ `fill_message` / `message_to_kwargs` بین protobuf و مدل تبدیل می‌کنند. * **Django**: `INSTALLED_APPS += ["aggify.contrib.django"]` و تنظیم `AGGIFY = {...}`؛ `get_object_or_404`، Paginator، فرم، میدلور تراکنش، و `ObjectIdField` برای نگه‌داشتن id مونگو داخل مدل‌های SQL جنگو. ## امنیت * **NoSQL injection**: مقدارها قبل از رسیدن به کوئری توسط نوع فیلد بررسی می‌شوند؛ `filter(username={"$ne": ""})` خطا می‌دهد. * **Regex**: `contains` و بقیه ورودی را escape می‌کنند؛ فقط `regex` صریح الگو می‌پذیرد (با سقف طول). * **JavaScript سمت سرور** (`$where`, `$function`, `$accumulator`) به‌صورت پیش‌فرض مسدود است. * نام فیلدها اعتبارسنجی می‌شوند، Mass-assignment با `TypeError` رد می‌شود، رمز URI در لاگ ماسک می‌شود. * سقف‌های قابل تنظیم: `max_limit`، `default_max_time_ms`، `max_in_list`. جزئیات کامل: [Security](security.md). ## تست `assert_num_queries(n)` و `capture_commands()` برای شمارش کوئری‌ها (مثل `assertNumQueries` جنگو)، `qs.query` / `pipeline.to_list()` برای تست بدون دیتابیس، و تست‌های differential با Hypothesis که ۲۵۰ کوئری تصادفی را با MongoDB واقعی و یک مرجع پایتونی مقایسه می‌کنند. جزئیات: [Testing](testing.md). ## مهاجرت * از MongoEngine: [راهنمای مهاجرت](migration/mongoengine.md) — داده‌ها سازگارند و می‌توان مدل‌به‌مدل مهاجرت کرد. * از Aggify نسخه‌ی 0.x: [تغییرات](migration/aggify-0.md).

docs.title: Documents
docs.text:
class Account(Document):
    username = StringField(required=True, unique=True, min_length=2, max_length=30)
    email = EmailField()
    role = EnumField(Role, default=Role.USER)
    tags = ListField(StringField())
    address = EmbeddedField(Address)          # an EmbeddedDocument
    manager = ReferenceField("Account")       # string = lazy / self reference
    created_at = DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    class Meta:
        collection = "accounts"
        ordering = ["username"]
        indexes = [Index("role", "-created_at"), Index("tags")]
  • The primary key is id (ObjectId, stored as _id) unless a field declares primary_key=True. obj.pk always works.
  • Documents are strict: Account(nope=1) raises TypeError (mass-assignment protection). Set Meta.strict = False or aggify.configure(strict_models=False) to ignore unknown keys.
  • Mutable defaults are safe: default=list / default=dict and any callable are evaluated per instance.
  • Values are converted when assigned (acc.age = "41" -> 41) and validated strictly on save() / full_clean().

None means absent

Fields set to None are not stored (and are $unset on update), so field=None filters match both missing and null values, and documents stay compact.

docs.text:
class Post(Document):
    owner = ReferenceField(Account, db_field="owner_id")

post.owner_id                # always available, never queries
post.owner                   # sync code: fetched on first access and cached
await post.afetch_related("owner")     # async code
Post.objects.select_related("owner")   # one query ($lookup)
Post.objects.prefetch_related("owner") # two queries ($in), good for many rows
Post.objects.filter(owner__country="DE")  # join happens automatically

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
save()/asave() insert new instances and send only changed fields for loaded ones; mutations in place (doc.tags.append("x"), doc.address.city = "y") are detected.

doc.save(update_fields=["age"])       # restrict the update
doc.save(validate=False)               # skip validation (values must already have the right types)
Model.objects.bulk_create(objs)        # insert_many in batches, validated up-front

Partial documents (only() / defer()) track and save just the fields that were loaded, so a partial save() can never wipe the rest of the document.

docs.title: Performance notes
docs.text:
• Writes are minimal: save() sends only changed fields. Use update_fields=[...] or queryset update() for hot paths; bulk_create() batches insert_many.
  • Reads: .only() / .defer() shrink documents; .values() / .values_list() skip model instantiation (about 30 % faster than instances in benchmarks/bench.py); iterator() / aiterator() stream huge results.
  • N+1: select_related("owner") (one $lookup) or prefetch_related("owner") (one extra $in query). Verify with assert_num_queries.
  • Counting: count() uses countDocuments; slices respect skip/limit. exists() fetches one _id.
  • Indexes: declare them, run ensure_indexes(), and check with qs.explain() that the plan is an IXSCAN. $lookup joins want an index on the foreign field (the target's _id for references - already indexed).
  • Pipelines: put selective filter() first; MongoDB also pushes $match before $lookup/$addFields when it is independent of them. Use options(allow_disk_use=True) for big sorts/groups.
  • Pooling: connect(..., maxPoolSize=..., minPoolSize=...) - one pool per event loop for async.
  • Overhead: instantiating a document costs roughly 3 us on top of the driver; compiling a typical queryset roughly 25 us. Run the benchmark yourself:
python benchmarks/bench.py mongodb://localhost:27017

Example output on a laptop (5 000 documents, local MongoDB):

read 5000 docs  raw pymongo (dicts)       7.5 ms
read 5000 docs  Aggify (instances)       16.3 ms
read 5000 docs  Aggify .values()         11.1 ms
group-by        raw pipeline              4.1 ms
group-by        Aggify                    4.3 ms

docs.title: Querying
docs.text: Model.objects returns a lazy, immutable QuerySet. Every chaining method returns a new queryset, so you can safely share and extend them. Nothing touches the database until you iterate, slice to an item, or call a terminal method (get, first, count, exists, aggregate, update, delete, ...). Each terminal method has an a-prefixed async twin.

docs.title: Filtering
docs.text:
Account.objects.filter(age__gte=18, country="DE")        # AND
Account.objects.exclude(banned=True)
Account.objects.filter(Q(vip=True) | Q(age__gt=60), ~Q(country="IR"))
Account.objects.filter(F("spent") > F("budget"))         # an expression as the condition
Account.objects.filter(age__gt=F("score") * 10)          # field vs expression

Multiple keyword arguments, chained filter() calls and & all mean AND. Conditions on the same field are merged into a single operator document when possible and into $and when not, so nothing is ever silently overwritten.

docs.title: Lookups
docs.text:
lookup example MongoDB (none) / exact name="x" {name: "x"} ne age__ne=3 $ne gt gte lt lte age__gte=18 $gt ... in / nin age__in=[1, 2] $in / $nin range age__range=(18, 30) $gte + $lte isnull deleted_at__isnull=True {f: null} (missing or null) exists meta__exists=True $exists contains / icontains name__icontains="al" escaped $regex startswith / istartswith name__startswith="a" ^… endswith / iendswith name__endswith="z" …$ iexact name__iexact="ALI" ^…$ with i regex / iregex name__regex=r"^a.+z$" $regex (explicit, length-capped) size tags__size=2 $size all tags__all=["a", "b"] $all elem_match items__elem_match=Q(qty__gte=5) $elemMatch type x__type="string" $type mod n__mod=(2, 0) $mod near location__near=(lng, lat, 5000) $near (find only)
  • Lists: tags="a" matches arrays that contain "a"; tags=["a", "b"] matches that exact array; tags__in, tags__contains... apply to the elements.
  • Embedded documents / dicts: address__city="Tehran", attrs__color="red", attrs__size__gt=3.
  • pk is an alias for the primary key: pk__in=[...].
  • contains-style lookups escape their input: name__contains=".*" searches for the literal text .*.

docs.title: Across references (automatic joins)
docs.text:
Post.objects.filter(owner__country="DE", owner__profile__verified=True)
Post.objects.order_by("-owner__created_at")
Post.objects.values("caption", "owner__name")
Order.objects.filter(items__product__category="toys")      # through a list of embedded docs

Aggify adds the $lookup/$unwind stages for you (aliased _j_<path>, never visible on your objects) and re-uses a join when several parts of the query need it. Filtering on the reference's id (owner=acc, owner__id=...) needs no join.

docs.text:
Account.objects.order_by("-age", "name")
Account.objects.order_by("-age").reverse()
qs[10:20]            # skip 10, limit 10          qs[:5]   qs[5:]   qs[3]
qs.first()  qs.last()  qs.latest("created_at")  qs.earliest("created_at")

Negative indexes and steps are rejected (MongoDB cannot do them cheaply). aggify.configure(max_limit=100) caps page sizes globally.

Account.objects.defer("big_blob")

docs.title: Aggregation, Django style
docs.text:
from aggify import Count, Sum, Avg, Max, Q

# whole queryset -> one dict
Order.objects.aggregate(n=Count(), revenue=Sum("total"), biggest=Max("total"),
                        paid=Sum("total", filter=Q(status="paid")))

# GROUP BY: values() + annotate(<aggregate>)
Order.objects.values("customer__country").annotate(n=Count(), revenue=Sum("total")).order_by("-revenue")

# HAVING: filter() after annotate() works on the aggregates; before it, it is a WHERE
(Order.objects.filter(status="paid")                 # WHERE
      .values("customer").annotate(n=Count())
      .filter(n__gte=3))                              # HAVING

# row-level computed fields
Account.objects.annotate(full=Concat("first", Value(" "), "last"), tags_n=Size("tags")).filter(tags_n__gt=2)

How grouping is decided

annotate() with an aggregate after values() groups by the values() fields (and expressions: values(day=DateToString("created_at", "%Y-%m-%d"))). Without values(), aggregates are evaluated per document as array operators (Size("items"), Sum("items__qty")). Meta.ordering is not applied to grouped queries, as in Django.

docs.text:
Account.objects.filter(age__lt=18).update(minor=True)             # update_many -> modified count
Account.objects.filter(pk=pk).update_one(inc__logins=1)
Account.objects.filter(email=e).update(upsert=True, name="New")
Account.objects.filter(...).delete()                              # delete_many (no per-doc signals)
Account.objects.bulk_create([...])

docs.text:
Post.objects.filter(pk=pk).update(
    title="New",                    # $set
    inc__views=1,                   # $inc
    push__tags="news",              # $push            push_all__tags=[...]
    add_to_set__tags="hot",         # $addToSet        add_to_set_all__tags=[...]
    pull__tags="old",               # $pull            pull_all__tags=[...]
    pop__tags=-1,                   # $pop

    unset__draft=True, rename__a="b", current_date__touched_at=True,

Product.objects.update(price=Round(F("price") * Value(1.1), 2), inc__stock=-1)

Assigning an expression switches to a MongoDB pipeline update; inc__, mul__, min__, max__, push__, add_to_set__ and unset__ are rewritten for you so they can be mixed in the same call.

import aggify

aggify.connect("mongodb://localhost:27017/library")        # database name from the URI
aggify.connect("mongodb+srv://...", "analytics", alias="analytics", maxPoolSize=50)  # a second database

SyncAsync 
Book.objects.create(title="Dune", author="Herbert", year=1965)

for book in old: ...
book = Book.objects.get(title="Dune")

Book.objects.filter(Q(author="Herbert") | Q(year__lt=1900))
Book.objects.exclude(author__in=["A", "B"]).count()

>>> Book.objects.filter(year__lt=1950).order_by("-year").query
{'find': {'filter': {'year': {'$lt': 1950}}, 'sort': [('year', -1)]}}

docs.text:
Declare them on fields (unique=True, index=True) or in Meta.indexes, then create them at start-up:

await Book.aensure_indexes()      # or Book.ensure_indexes()

The complete runnable version of this page is docs/examples/quickstart.py (it is part of the test-suite).

"""Quickstart used by docs/tutorial/quickstart.md (executed by the test-suite)."""

import asyncio

import aggify
from aggify import Count, Document, IntField, Q, StringField


class Book(Document):
    title = StringField(required=True)
    author = StringField()
    year = IntField(min_value=0)

    class Meta:
        collection = "books"
        ordering = ["year"]


def sync_demo():
    Book.drop_collection()
    Book.objects.create(title="Dune", author="Herbert", year=1965)
    Book.objects.bulk_create(
        [Book(title="Emma", author="Austen", year=1815), Book(title="Ulysses", author="Joyce", year=1922)]
    )
    old = Book.objects.filter(year__lt=1950).order_by("-year")
    assert [b.title for b in old] == ["Ulysses", "Emma"]
    assert Book.objects.filter(Q(author="Herbert") | Q(year__lt=1900)).count() == 2
    book = Book.objects.get(title="Dune")
    book.year = 1966
    book.save()  # only {"$set": {"year": 1966}} is sent
    assert Book.objects.aggregate(first=aggify.Min("year"), n=Count()) == {"first": 1815, "n": 3}
    return True


async def async_demo():
    book = await Book.objects.acreate(title="Neuromancer", year=1984)
    assert await Book.objects.filter(year__gt=1980).acount() == 1
    async for b in Book.objects.filter(year__lt=1930):
        assert b.year < 1930
    await book.adelete()
    return True


def run():
    assert sync_demo()
    assert asyncio.run(async_demo())
    return True

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
Connection registry.

  • connect(...) only registers settings - clients are created lazily, so importing your models never touches the network.
  • One synchronous MongoClient per alias (thread-safe).
  • One AsyncMongoClient per alias per running event loop (pymongo's async client is bound to its loop), which makes the library safe in FastAPI/uvicorn workers, gRPC aio servers, Django's async_to_sync and pytest-asyncio.
  • Transactions are carried in a ContextVar so every query in the block joins the session automatically, in threads and asyncio tasks alike.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Aggify is designed so that the easy way to write a query is also the safe one. This page lists the threats it addresses, what it does about each, and what remains your responsibility.

docs.title: 1. NoSQL operator injection
docs.text:
The classic attack: a handler does User.find({"username": body["username"]}) and the client posts {"username": {"$ne": ""}} - logging in as anyone.

In Aggify every value is converted by its field before it can reach a query:

User.objects.filter(username=request_json["username"])      # {"$ne": ""} -> ValidationError("Expected a string.")
User.objects.filter(age__in=request_json["ages"])            # a dict / string instead of a list -> error
User.objects.filter(attrs__color=request_json["c"])           # untyped value: any "$" key anywhere -> UnsafeQueryError
  • StringField accepts only str, IntField only int (not bool), ObjectIdField only 24-hex ids...
  • For untyped fields (DictField, AnyField, computed columns) values are scanned recursively and any mapping with a $-prefixed key is refused (UnsafeQueryError).
  • Q() rejects dicts: there is no way to smuggle an operator document through Q({...}).
  • Raw(...) is the one explicit escape hatch - grep for it in code review.
  • Model(**request_json) raises TypeError for unknown keys (mass assignment) - unless you disable strict.
  • Update operators validate their operands (inc__x="5", push__tags={"$each": ...} fail), and the primary key cannot be updated.

Pair it with request validation

For HTTP/gRPC input use pydantic_model(Model, for_input=True) (forbids extra keys, enforces types and limits) and let Aggify's field validation be the second line of defence.

docs.title: 2. Regular-expression injection and ReDoS
docs.text: contains, startswith, endswith, iexact and friends escape the user's text: name__contains="(a+)+$" searches for that literal text. Only the explicit regex / iregex lookups accept a pattern; they are length-capped (max_regex_length, default 256) and must compile.

docs.title: 3. Server-side JavaScript
docs.text:
$where, $function and $accumulator run JavaScript inside mongod. They are rejected in filters, raw stages, Raw(...) and nested pipelines (SecurityError) unless you opt in:

aggify.configure(allow_javascript=True)      # strongly discouraged

docs.title: 4. Field and path injection
docs.text: Field names used as paths (annotation names, $out collections, dictionary keys, rename__) are validated: no $ prefix, no NUL, no empty segments. DictField keys may not start with $ or contain .. Filter paths must exist on the model (typos raise InvalidField instead of silently matching nothing); inside dictionaries a $-segment (attrs__$where) is refused.

docs.title: 5. Resource exhaustion
docs.text:
setting default effect max_limit None largest allowed limit() / slice (set it on public APIs) max_in_list 100 000 longest __in / __nin / __all list max_regex_length 256 longest user-supplied regex max_value_depth 64 nesting depth of untyped values default_max_time_ms None applied to every find/aggregate/count (maxTimeMS) 
aggify.configure(max_limit=200, default_max_time_ms=5_000)

qs.options(max_time_ms=...) and pipeline.options(max_time_ms=..., allow_disk_use=...) override per query.

docs.title: 6. Credentials and logging
docs.text: connect() returns a config whose repr() masks the password (mongodb://user:***@host/db); the URI is never included in exception messages. Prefer environment variables or a secrets manager for the URI, enable TLS (mongodb+srv:// or ?tls=true) and give the application user the minimum roles it needs.

docs.title: 7. Data integrity
docs.text:
• Strict types: bool is not an int, Decimal is stored exactly (Decimal128), datetimes are UTC and timezone aware, NaN decimals are rejected, integers are range-checked against 64 bits.
  • save() writes only changed fields, optional optimistic locking prevents lost updates.
  • Transactions (replica set) for multi-document invariants.
  • unique=True creates unique indexes (ensure_indexes()); violations surface as NotUniqueError.

docs.title: What is still on you
docs.text:
• Authentication/authorisation: Aggify filters data, it does not decide whose data to filter. Scope querysets by tenant/user in a custom Manager.get_queryset().
  • Network exposure and MongoDB hardening (bind addresses, authentication, TLS, backups).
  • Anything you pass through Raw(...), Pipeline.stage() / raw() or allow_javascript=True.
  • Rate limiting and pagination limits on public endpoints.

Found a vulnerability? See SECURITY.md.

docs.title: How Aggify tests itself
docs.text:
• Unit tests (no database): fields, lookups, Q, expressions, pipeline stages, update building, security rules.
  • Integration tests against a real replica set: CRUD, joins, grouping, transactions, signals, indexes (and that queries really use them), multiple event loops and threads, 40 concurrent requests...
  • Differential tests (tests/integration/test_differential.py): Hypothesis generates random documents and random Q trees (AND/OR/NOT over 20+ lookups); the same predicate is evaluated by MongoDB through Aggify and by a small Python reference implementation - results must be identical, and exclude() must be the exact complement.
  • Property tests for security: no string field can ever emit a $-keyed value; escaped regexes match literally.
  • Framework tests: a real FastAPI app over ASGI (including injection attempts and transactions), an in-process grpc.aio server, Django views (sync and async), forms, pagination, management command, middleware.
  • The runnable documentation examples are executed too.
make mongo          # throw-away replica set in Docker on :27018
make test           # pytest
make test-all       # + lint, mypy, 3.9 - 3.13 via tox

Set AGGIFY_TEST_MONGO_URI to use another server; tests marked mongo skip themselves when none is reachable and tests marked replica skip on a standalone server.

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text:
Multi-document transactions need a replica set (or sharded cluster); a standalone mongod rejects them.

with aggify.transaction():
    order = Order.objects.create(...)
    Product.objects.filter(pk=pid).update(inc__stock=-1)
    # exception -> rollback, otherwise commit

async with aggify.atransaction():
    order = await Order.objects.acreate(...)
    await Product.objects.filter(pk=pid).aupdate(inc__stock=-1)
  • The session lives in a ContextVar: every query, save(), bulk_create(), delete()... executed inside the block - in the same thread or asyncio task - joins the transaction automatically. Separate tasks that each open their own atransaction() get independent transactions.
  • A MongoDB session is not safe for concurrent operations: inside one transaction run statements one after another (do not asyncio.gather queries that share the same transaction).
  • Nested blocks join the outer transaction (no savepoints in MongoDB).
  • transaction(alias="other", read_concern=..., write_concern=...) forwards options to start_transaction.
  • Collections must exist before concurrent transactions touch them for the first time (MongoDB cannot create the same collection from two transactions at once): run ensure_indexes() at start-up.
  • aggify.current_session() returns the active ClientSession (or None).

In Django, AggifyAtomicMiddleware wraps each request (sync or async); in FastAPI use Depends(transaction_dependency).

docs.title: Django
docs.text:
Aggify's Django support is optional and does not make Django a dependency of the core.

pip install "aggify[django]"

# settings.py

AGGIFY = {
    "default": {"URI": "mongodb://localhost:27017", "NAME": "shop", "OPTIONS": {"maxPoolSize": 50}},
    "analytics": {"URI": "mongodb+srv://...", "NAME": "stats"},      # models choose with Meta.db_alias
}
AGGIFY_SETTINGS = {"default_max_time_ms": 5000, "max_limit": 500}     # optional, see Security
# or simply: MONGODB_URI = "mongodb://localhost/shop"

AggifyConfig.ready() registers the connections. Documents live anywhere you like (app/documents.py, models.py).

docs.text:
# sync view
from aggify.contrib.django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404, aget_object_or_404, get_list_or_404

def detail(request, username):
    account = get_object_or_404(Account, username=username)
    ...

# async view (Django >= 4.1)
async def stats(request):
    rows = await Order.objects.values("status").annotate(n=Count()).alist()
    return JsonResponse({"rows": rows})
  • Model.objects, Model.DoesNotExist, Q, F, get_or_create, update_or_create, in_bulk, signals, managers.
  • Pagination: django.core.paginator.Paginator(Account.objects.order_by("username"), 25) works as is (count() + slicing).
  • Forms: document_form(Account, fields=["username", "age"]) builds a django.forms.Form; form.save() / await form.asave() validate through the document and persist it; pass instance= to edit.
  • Management command: python manage.py aggify_indexes [Model ...] creates the declared indexes.
  • Transactions per request (replica set): add "aggify.contrib.django.middleware.AggifyAtomicMiddleware"; it works for WSGI and ASGI.
  • Tests: nothing special; use a throw-away database (aggify.testing.temporary_database).

docs.title: Connecting to the Django ORM
docs.text:
Mix SQL and Mongo in one project by storing Mongo ids in Django models, and Django pks in documents:

from aggify.contrib.django.fields import ObjectIdField

class Invoice(models.Model):                      # PostgreSQL / MySQL / SQLite
    customer = ObjectIdField(db_index=True)       # Mongo Customer._id (24-char column, returns bson.ObjectId)
    total = models.DecimalField(max_digits=12, decimal_places=2)

customer = await Customer.objects.aget(pk=invoice.customer)

class Event(Document):
    user_id = IntField(index=True)                # Django auth user pk
    payload = DictField()

Event.objects.filter(user_id=request.user.pk)

Use Document.to_dict(json_safe=True) for DRF/JSON responses, or pydantic_model for schema-based APIs (django-ninja accepts Pydantic models directly).

docs.title: Sync, async and WSGI/ASGI
docs.text: Under WSGI (gunicorn sync workers) use the sync API. Under ASGI use the a* methods in async views and the sync API in sync views (Django runs those in a thread). Aggify keeps one async client per event loop, so async_to_sync / sync_to_async boundaries are safe.

docs.title: FastAPI
docs.text:
Aggify is plain asyncio with no thread-locals, so it fits FastAPI as is. aggify.contrib.fastapi adds the glue.

pip install "aggify[fastapi]"

from typing import Optional
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from aggify.contrib.fastapi import Page, Pagination, get_or_404, install_exception_handlers, lifespan, paginate
from aggify.contrib.pydantic import pydantic_model

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan("mongodb://localhost:27017", "shop", indexes=[Account]))
install_exception_handlers(app)

AccountIn = pydantic_model(Account, name="AccountIn", for_input=True)          # request body
AccountPatch = pydantic_model(Account, name="AccountPatch", for_input=True, all_optional=True)
AccountOut = pydantic_model(Account, name="AccountOut", exclude=["attrs"])      # response

@app.post("/accounts", response_model=AccountOut, status_code=201)
async def create(body: AccountIn):
    return await Account.objects.acreate(**body.model_dump(exclude_unset=True))

@app.get("/accounts", response_model=Page[AccountOut])
async def listing(page: Pagination = Depends(), q: Optional[str] = None):
    qs = Account.objects.filter(username__icontains=q) if q else Account.objects.all()
    return await paginate(qs, page)             # {"items": [...], "total": n, "limit": .., "offset": ..}

@app.get("/accounts/{pk}", response_model=AccountOut)
async def read(pk: str):
    return await get_or_404(Account.objects, pk=pk)     # malformed ids are a 404, not a 500

@app.patch("/accounts/{pk}", response_model=AccountOut)
async def patch(pk: str, body: AccountPatch):
    obj = await get_or_404(Account.objects, pk=pk)
    for key, value in body.model_dump(exclude_unset=True).items():
        setattr(obj, key, value)
    await obj.asave()                                      # only the changed fields are written
    return obj

docs.title: What the helpers do
docs.text: helper lifespan(uri, db, indexes=[...]) connects, pings, creates indexes at start-up; closes the loop's clients on shutdown install_exception_handlers(app) ValidationError->422 (with per-field errors), DoesNotExist->404, NotUniqueError/OptimisticLockError->409, SecurityError/InvalidField/InvalidLookup->400 get_or_404(qs, **filters) await qs.aget(...) or HTTPException(404) Pagination, paginate(qs, page), Page[T] limit (1-200) / offset query params and the response envelope transaction_dependency dependencies=[Depends(transaction_dependency)] wraps the request in a transaction (replica set)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• pydantic_model() builds the schemas from the document, including constraints (max_length, ge, pattern, max_digits), embedded documents, enums and ObjectId (24-hex string in JSON). for_input=True drops the primary key and server-managed fields and forbids unknown keys.
  • Do not call blocking methods in async def endpoints - Aggify refuses with SynchronousOnlyOperation. In plain def endpoints (FastAPI runs them in a thread pool) the sync API is fine.
  • Several uvicorn/gunicorn workers: each process has its own loop and therefore its own pool.
  • Testing: httpx.AsyncClient(transport=ASGITransport(app=app)) and app.router.lifespan_context(app); see tests/contrib/test_fastapi.py.

docs.title: gRPC
docs.text:
Aggify works unchanged inside grpc.aio servicers: there is no per-thread state, clients are per event loop, and transactions use ContextVars that follow each RPC's task.

pip install "aggify[grpc]"

import grpc
from aggify.contrib.grpc import grpc_errors, fill_message, message_to_kwargs

class AccountService(accounts_pb2_grpc.AccountsServicer):

    @grpc_errors                       # Aggify errors -> proper gRPC status codes
    async def Get(self, request, context):
        account = await Account.objects.aget(pk=request.id)
        return fill_message(accounts_pb2.Account(), account)

    @grpc_errors
    async def Create(self, request, context):
        account = await Account.objects.acreate(**message_to_kwargs(request))
        return fill_message(accounts_pb2.Account(), account)

    @grpc_errors
    async def Search(self, request, context):             # server streaming
        async for acc in Account.objects.filter(username__icontains=request.q).aiterator():
            yield fill_message(accounts_pb2.Account(), acc)


async def serve():
    aggify.connect("mongodb://localhost:27017/shop")
    await Account.aensure_indexes()
    server = grpc.aio.server()
    accounts_pb2_grpc.add_AccountsServicer_to_server(AccountService(), server)
    server.add_insecure_port("[::]:50051")
    await server.start()
    try:
        await server.wait_for_termination()
    finally:
        await aggify.adisconnect()

docs.title: Status code mapping
docs.text: Aggify gRPC ValidationError, SecurityError, InvalidField, QueryError INVALID_ARGUMENT Model.DoesNotExist NOT_FOUND NotUniqueError ALREADY_EXISTS OptimisticLockError ABORTED ConnectionNotConfigured UNAVAILABLE anything else propagates (gRPC reports UNKNOWN)

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
• doc.to_dict(json_safe=True, include=[...], exclude=[...], include_none=False) produces only JSON/protobuf friendly primitives (ObjectId/UUID/Decimal as strings, datetimes as ISO-8601) - feed it to google.protobuf.json_format.ParseDict. fill_message does exactly that.
  • message_to_kwargs(msg) goes the other way using the proto field names, ready for Model(**kwargs) - which rejects unknown keys.
  • For google.protobuf.Timestamp fields convert explicitly (Timestamp().FromDatetime(doc.created_at)).

See tests/contrib/test_grpc.py for a complete in-process server (generic handlers, no protoc needed).

docs.title: Pydantic
docs.text:
from aggify.contrib.pydantic import pydantic_model, to_pydantic, from_pydantic, PyObjectId

Out = pydantic_model(Account, name="AccountOut", exclude=["password_hash"])
In = pydantic_model(Account, name="AccountIn", for_input=True)
Patch = pydantic_model(Account, name="AccountPatch", for_input=True, all_optional=True)

to_pydantic(account, Out)          # document -> model
from_pydantic(Account, body)       # model -> unsaved document (unset fields stay default)

Mapping: StringField(max_length=..)->str + constraints, IntField(min_value=..)->ge/le, DecimalField->Decimal with digits, ListField->List[...], DictField->Dict[str, ...], EmbeddedField->nested model, ReferenceField->PyObjectId, EnumField->the enum, GeoPointField->Tuple[float, float].

PyObjectId validates 24-hex strings, serialises as a string in JSON and renders as {"type": "string", "pattern": "^[0-9a-fA-F]{24}$"} in OpenAPI.

Models are cached per (document, options), so calling pydantic_model in several modules is cheap. Documents can also be read by Pydantic directly (from_attributes=True).

docs.title: Upgrading from Aggify 0.x
docs.text:
Aggify 0.x was a pipeline generator for MongoEngine models. 1.0 is a standalone ODM: the pipeline builder is still here (from aggify import Aggify) but it works on Aggify documents and no longer depends on MongoEngine.

0.x 1.0 from mongoengine import Document, fields from aggify import Document, StringField, ... Aggify(Model) mutated and returned self immutable: each call returns a new pipeline list(pipeline) -> stages still works (__iter__); pipeline.to_list() is explicit [start:stop] and [n] (n = limit n) slicing as in Django; [n] is the n-th document ($skip n, $limit 1) .filter(a__exact=1, b__contains="x") same; contains & co. now escape the value lookups added as_name = the reference field (overwriting the id) joins use hidden _j_<field> aliases .lookup(Model, let=["id"], query=[Q(end__exact="id")], ...) docs.title: Bugs fixed on the way
docs.text:
• contains/startswith... put raw user text into a regex (regex injection / ReDoS).
  • $subtract / $divide with three operands (rejected by MongoDB), mutation of shared F/Q objects.
  • convert_match_query missed $ in $lte; the let substitution replaced any equal-looking value in a query.
  • $unwind used the local field name instead of the alias after joins.
  • Consecutive $match stages with the same key silently dropped the first condition.
  • [n] meant "limit n".

docs.title: Moving your models
docs.text:
# before
from mongoengine import Document, fields
class Account(Document):
    username = fields.StringField()
    meta = {"collection": "account"}

# after
from aggify import Document, StringField
class Account(Document):
    username = StringField()
    class Meta:
        collection = "account"

Then Aggify(Account).filter(...)... keeps working, and you gain Account.objects, async execution (await pipeline.aexecute()) and validation. The comparison table in the MongoEngine guide covers the rest of the model API.

docs.title: Migrating from MongoEngine
docs.text: Aggify is not a fork of MongoEngine: documents, fields and queries were re-designed (async, immutable querysets, strict validation). The data stays compatible - same collections, same BSON - so you can migrate model by model.

docs.title: Behavioural differences to know about
docs.text:
1. Querysets are immutable - qs.filter(...) returns a new queryset (MongoEngine's __call__ mutated in place).
  2. Strict types: StringField no longer coerces 5 to "5"; filter(name={"$ne": ""}) raises instead of running. Conversions are lenient only where unambiguous ("5" -> 5, 24-hex -> ObjectId).
  3. None is stored as "absent" (as MongoEngine did) - filter(x=None) matches missing and null.
  4. Unknown constructor kwargs raise (strict), unknown stored keys are ignored on load.
  5. Datetimes are always timezone-aware UTC.
  6. Dirty tracking is value-based: in-place mutation of lists/dicts/embedded documents is detected, and save() updates only changed fields.
  7. No allow_inheritance / _cls (polymorphic documents) yet. Keep such collections on MongoEngine or model them with a discriminator field and abstract bases.
  8. References are not auto-dereferenced: use select_related, prefetch_related or afetch_related. Lazy sync access works outside event loops.
  9. DictField keys cannot start with $ or contain ..
  10. GenericReferenceField, GridFS, SequenceField, CachedReferenceField, LazyReferenceField are not provided.

docs.title: A suggested path
docs.text:
1. Install Aggify next to MongoEngine; both can talk to the same database.
  2. Re-declare one model with Aggify (same collection, same db_fields). Document the indexes with Index - ensure_indexes() is a no-op for indexes that already exist with the same definition.
  3. Move its call sites over. The sync API is deliberately close to MongoEngine's; the async API comes for free.
  4. Replace hand-built aggregate([...]) calls with querysets/pipelines using the cookbook.
  5. Delete the MongoEngine model.
